item.title: 11. Matrix Inverses and Determinants
item.description:
Invertibility and determinants tell us when $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ has a unique solution and give explicit formulas (Cramer, adjugate) and algorithms (Gauss–Jordan).

Invertibility conditions ($n \times n$)

$A$ is invertible (non-singular) iff any (hence all) of:

  • $\det(A) \neq 0$.
  • $\text{rank}(A) = n$.
  • Columns (and rows) are linearly independent.
  • $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$ has only the trivial solution $\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$.
  • $A$ is row-equivalent to $I$.
  • $0$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$.
  • $A^T A$ is positive definite.

Gauss–Jordan elimination

To find $A^{-1}$: form $[A \mid I]$, apply row operations until $A$ becomes $I$; then $[I \mid A^{-1}]$. Elementary row operations (EROs): row swap, multiply row by nonzero scalar, add a multiple of one row to another.
